., And Another vs Bommisetty Shiva Shankar on 21
February, 2023
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice V.Gopala Krishna Rao
 M.A.C.M.A.No.1234 of 2012
Judgement:
The appellants are the respondents in M.V.O.P.No.152of 2009 on the file of the Motor Vehicles
Accidents Claims Tribunal (Principal District Judge), Kadapa, and the respondent is the petitioner
in the said case.
2. Both the parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in claim application.

3. The petitioner filed a Claim Petition under section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act against the respondents, praying the Tribunal to award an amount of Rs.1,50,000/- towards compensation on account of injuries received by him in a Motor Vehicles Accident occurred on 14.10.2008at 3.30 PM.

4. The case of the petitioner is that on 14.10.2008 at about 3.30 p.m. the petitioner, aged about 7 years, along with his mother and sister got down the mini bus at Buddareddigaripalli village and when the petitioner was proceeding towards his house after he alighted VGKRJ MACMA 1234 of 2012 the bus, the driver of APSRTC bus bearing No.AP 11Z3497, drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner, resulting which, the petitioner sustained grievous injuriesand the petitioner claimed an amount of Rs.1,50,000/- towards compensation.
5.
The first respondent remained exparte.

The second respondent filed counter denying the claim application and contended that the claimant is not entitled any compensation and the second respondent isnot liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.

6. Based on the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues:
i.

Whether the accidentoccurred on account of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the vehicle bearing No.AP 11Z 3497 and whether the respondents 1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to answer the claim?
ii. If so, what is the quantum of compensation that the petitioner is entitled to and who are liable to pay compensation?
iii. To what relief?
VGKRJ MACMA 1234 of 2012 7.
On behalf of the petitioner,PW1 to PW3 were examined and Ex.A1 to Ex.A5 were marked.
No oral or documentary evidence was adduced on behalf of respondents.

9. Aggrieved by the same, the respondents/appellants filed the present appeal.

10. Now, the points for consideration are:
1) Whether theaccident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of APSRTC bus bearing No.AP 11Z 3497?
2) Whether the Order of Tribunal needs any interference?
11. POINT Nos.1 and 2:-
The case of the petitioner is that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of APSRTC bus bearing No.AP 11Z 3497.

The learned Standing Counsel for VGKRJ MACMA 1234 of 2012 APSRTC contended that the driver of the bus drove the bus carefully and in a slow manner and there is no negligence on the part of the driver of RTC bus.
PW1 is none other than the father of the minor petitioner.
PW2 is eye witness to the accident.
The evidence of PW2 supports the case of the petitioner.
The petitioner in order to prove the rashness and negligent driving of the driver of RTC bus relied on Ex.A1 certified copy of FIR and Ex.A3 certified copy of charge sheet.

The complaint lodged by the mother of the claim petitioner was registered as FIR and the case of the petitioner is that on 14.10.2008 himself along with his mother and sister by name Sravani travelled in a mini bus from Rayachoty to Buddareddigaripalli and got down the bus at 3.30 p.m. and while proceeding towards their house, the driver of APSRTC bus bearing No.AP 11Z 3497 proceeding towards Sattipalli, drove the bus in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner and that petitioner sustained fracture injuries.
12 . The evidence of PW2 coupled with Ex.A1 and Ex.A3 clearly goes to show that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of APSRTC bus.
After completion of investigation VGKRJ MACMA 1234 of 2012 by the investigating officer, the police filed charge sheet against the driver of APSRTC bus in a criminal case.

The evidence on record clearly proves that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of APSRTC bus bearing No.AP 11Z 3497.
13.
The contention of the petitioner is that in a road accident which was caused by the driver of offending vehicle, he sustained fracture injuries and relied on Ex.A2.

Ex.A2 wound certificate discloses that the petitioner sustained three injuries, out of which, injury No.2 is grievous in nature and to prove the disability, the claimant relied on the evidence of PW3, who was the member of the District Medical Board.
As per the evidence of PW3, the injured sustained fracture injury and Apsrtc., And Another vs Bommisetty Shiva Shankar on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105353386/

sentences.text: 2 disability of 25% was estimated.
PW3 also certified that there was a deformity of the right leg and the gait of the petitioner was not in proper.

On considering the oral evidence of PW3 and on considering the disability certificate, the learned Tribunal by assigning the reasons, came to conclusion that the petitioner is suffering with disability of 15%, therefore, there is no need to interfere with the said finding given by the Tribunal.
VGKRJ MACMA 1234 of 2012 14. In this case the claimant sustained three injuries, out of which, one injury is grievous in nature.

The trial Court granted compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards pain and suffering and the said amount granted by Tribunal is just and reasonable and the learned Tribunal also granted Rs.30,000/- towards partial permanent disability.

On considering the material evidence on record,
this Court came to conclusion that there is no need to interfere with the said finding given by the Tribunal.

The learned Tribunal also granted an amount of Rs.3,000/- towards extra nourishment,
Rs.1,000/- towards medical expenses and Rs.2,000/- towards transportation charges.

The Tribunal below by assigning reasons granted total compensation of Rs.76,000/- together with interest at 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit and it was also held by the tribunal that both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the claim to the petitioner.
The trial Court rightly allowed in-part and granted compensation of Rs.76,000/- by giving cogent reasons.

This Court also perused the material available on record, on scrutinizing the same, this Court came to conclusion that there is no need to interfere with the finding given by VGKRJ MACMA 1234 of 2012 the Tribunal below.
Therefore, in view of the above reasons, the appeal is devoid of merits.
15. In the result, the appeal is dismissed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this appeal shall stand closed.

V.GOPALA KRISHNA RAO,J Dated: 21.02.2023.
